title: Tail Concerto
subtitle: A policeman among floating islands

body: Tail Concerto is CyberConnect's first game, an action-adventure released for PlayStation in Japan on 16 April 1998. Waffle Ryebread, a young canine policeman, pilots a Police Robo through the floating islands of Prairie. His encounters with the Black Cats Gang connect small disturbances to a search for dangerous crystals. Airships, steam machinery and ancient ruins give the world its setting, while dogs and cats supply its inhabitants. Nobuteru Yūki's character designs help the machines and expressive animal cast belong to the same light-hearted adventure, even as their disagreements reveal deeper tensions.

The Police Robo runs, jumps, climbs ledges and briefly hovers. Its mechanical arms lift and throw objects, while a bubble blaster immobilises enemies at a distance. Capturing troublesome kittens therefore involves getting close enough to grab them, not simply firing until they disappear. Objectives change between stages, with mine carts, a jet pack and guided missiles supplying other ways to travel or fight. The large machine becomes an adaptable body for Waffle: each tool changes how he crosses a place and what he can do when he reaches its inhabitants.

Towns allow Waffle to talk with residents between the action stages. Hidden whistles grant extra lives, and boxes contain fragments of pictures that become viewable in a gallery when assembled. These discoveries give corners of the islands another purpose beyond the current police assignment. Chikayo Fukuda and Seizo Nakata composed the music; the Japanese opening uses Kokia's For Little Tail. A French release followed in 1998 and an English North American edition in 1999. Despite an encouraging critical response, Japanese sales fell short of expectations, leaving the setting as a smaller, distinctive PlayStation adventure.
